findings.explanation: The GET /webhook handler that verifies Facebook's webhook subscription challenge compares the client-supplied hub.verify_token directly against the secret fbVerifyToken using plain === instead of crypto.timingSafeEqual. String === short-circuits on the first differing byte, leaking timing information that lets an attacker incrementally brute-force the token. This is inconsistent with the rest of the codebase: the POST /webhook handler right below it (verifySignature, line 276) correctly uses crypto.timingSafeEqual for the HMAC signature, and admin-auth.js's safeEqualSecret / admin/session.js's safeEqualText both hash-then-timingSafeEqual before comparing secrets.
